title: Austronesian settlement of Madagascar
summary: Madagascar's people combine African ancestry with Austronesian-speaking settlers who came across the Indian Ocean. The date is disputed: a late first millennium BC settlement was once increasingly accepted, but a 2019 review finds no convincing evidence before the mid-first millennium AD. Asian crops such as rice and mung bean at sites dated about 650-1200 CE give the first archaeobotanical trace.

uncertainty.note: Years are astronomical (AD = same number). Start 500 reflects Mitchell (2019): no convincing evidence before the "mid-first millennium AD". End 1200 is the upper limit of the 18 crop sites (about 650-1200 cal CE) in Crowther et al. 2016. Earlier claims (late first millennium BC; stone tools at Lakaton'i Anja; cut-marked bones at Christmas River and Lamboharana) are rejected by Mitchell and not included in the range. The id year -0100 reflects the earlier BC view.
